2608.07077.title: Transformers Struggle to Use Their Emergent World Models: Revisiting the Tower of Hanoi, and the Illusion of Thinking
2608.07077.paper_summary: The Tower of Hanoi is a simple planning puzzle that in prior work has proven challenging for large reasoning models (LRMs). Current models solve the standard formulation of the puzzle, but still struggle with the flat-to-flat variant (where initial and goal states are not restricted to have all rings on a single peg). This paper presents an in-depth study of how both small, in-house Transformers and large, third-party LRMs solve this task. To understand the failures mechanistically, we first train small Transformers from scratch on precomputed solution traces. Using a variety of interpretability techniques, we show that these Transformers develop an emergent world model: a linearly decodable, geometrically faithful representation of the puzzle's state space (the Sierpinski triangle), that is causally involved in solving the puzzles. Second, we return to the large LLMs and apply our techniques to two frontier reasoning models, Qwen3.6-27B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, that attempt to solve the task through extended chain-of-thought. Surprisingly, we find that both models encode the Sierpinski world model near-perfectly at the end of the prompt, and yet fail at the majority of tasks when there are more than 3 rings. We locate the source of this failure in the decaying representation of the world model. We probe for the representation at different stages during planning, and establish causality by showing that performance can be improved by injecting the prompt-time representation at inference. The failure of the models is thus one of maintenance of the required representations, not their absence, and performance is at least partially recoverable. These results thus reframe the reported collapse in performance from prior work: current Large Reasoning Models build a world model, and then lose it.
2608.07077.paper_summary_zh: 河內塔是一個簡單的規劃謎題，在先前的研究中對大型推理模型（LRMs）來說一直是個挑戰。當前的模型能夠解決謎題的標準形式，但在平面到平面的變體（即初始狀態和目標狀態不限制所有環都在同一根柱子上）上仍然掙扎。本文深入研究了小型內部Transformer和大型第三方LRMs如何解決這一任務。為了機械性地理解失敗，我們首先從頭開始訓練小型Transformer，使用預計算的解決方案痕跡。通過各種可解釋性技術，我們顯示這些Transformer發展出一種新興的世界模型：一種線性可解碼、幾何上忠實的謎題狀態空間表示（謝爾賓斯基三角形），在解決謎題中具有因果關係。其次，我們回到大型LLMs，並將我們的技術應用於兩個前沿推理模型，Qwen3.6-27B和DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B，這些模型試圖通過擴展的思考鏈來解決任務。令人驚訝的是，我們發現這兩個模型在提示結束時幾乎完美地編碼了謝爾賓斯基世界模型，但在環數超過3個時卻在大多數任務中失敗。我們將這一失敗的根源定位於世界模型的衰退表示。我們在規劃的不同階段探查表示，並通過顯示在推理時注入提示時間表示可以改善性能來建立因果關係。因此，模型的失敗是維持所需表示的問題，而不是它們的缺失，性能至少在某種程度上是可恢復的。因此，這些結果重新框架了先前工作中報告的性能崩潰：當前的大型推理模型建立了一個世界模型，然後又失去了它。
2608.07077.author: Devin Pereira et.al.
